title: Changing the Shape of Materials
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Changing the Shape of Materials Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Recognise that materials can be changed physically without changing their material composition and explore the effect of different actions on materials including bending, twisting, stretching and breaking into smaller pieces (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on changing the shape of materials: bending, twisting, stretching and squashing, materials that spring back, and why the material stays the same. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Bending, twisting, stretching and squashing change the shape, not the material.
body_html:
How to think about it

We can change the shape of materials.

  • Bend, twist, stretch, squash or fold.
  • Rubber springs back; play dough does not.
  • It is still the same material.
Example

Bent paperclip: still metal?

only the shape changed

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bent or squashed object is a new material.
  • Thinking all materials spring back.

faq.a: A physical change changes the shape or size of a material but not what it is made of.

faq.q: Why do some materials spring back?
faq.a: Materials like rubber and sponge are elastic: they return to their shape after being stretched or squashed.
Squash play dough, stretch rubber bands, fold paper and twist pipe cleaners, then talk about what changed.
